thread:
tara: Quick sync — thinking about adding a tier-specific 'fallback budget' and strict quota signal for routing. We need to decide console UX + API semantics. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

mike: can you sketch the concrete problem we're solving? is this about free accounts hitting qps or cost/time-to-first-byte?

tara: both. Free should fall back aggressively to cheaper variants and maybe regional replicas, pro should prefer low-latency variants but tolerate occasional fallback, enterprise gets pinned variants + hard quota enforcement. Also need a clear telemetry event for when fallback is used so support can debug.

raj: +1. infra wants a single routing policy object that includes per-tier overrides and a fallback chain. example idea: YAML config in control plane that looks like:

```yaml
policy_name: default_by_tier
tiers:
  free:
    preferred_models: [redwood-small-v1, open-3b-q8]
    fallback_chain: [open-3b-q8, redwood-tiny]
    fallback_budget: 0.6 # fraction of requests allowed to fallback per minute
    quota_enforcement: soft
  pro:
    preferred_models: [redwood-med-v1]
    fallback_chain: [redwood-small-v1]
    fallback_budget: 0.1
    quota_enforcement: best_effort
  enterprise:
    preferred_models: [redwood-large-v2]
    fallback_chain: []
    fallback_budget: 0.0
    quota_enforcement: hard
```

sarah: UI concern — showing a "fallback budget" slider for each tier might be confusing. Maybe show a simple toggle for "allow fallbacks" and an advanced section for the budget + per-region overrides. We should default to conservative values.

eliz: for SRE / incidents, we need strong telemetry keys. propose these events: route_decision, quota_breach, fallback_used, fallback_budget_exhausted, model_unavailable. Add dimensions: tier, region, tenant_id, request_latency_ms, model_variant.

mike: API impact: how does this map to the routing decision endpoint? we have /v1/routing/decide currently returning model_id + node. Should we return an array like [{model, reason, variant_hint}] if fallback was applied? clients might rely on single model field.

raj: I'd prefer keeping it backward compatible: keep model field but add optional metadata.routes which is an array of fallback steps and the telemetry_id. example response snippet in the control plane API:

```json
{"model": "redwood-small-v1", "metadata.routes": [{"model":"open-3b-q8","reason":"budget_fallback"}], "telemetry_id": "rtd-2026-06-01-123"}
```

tara: UX for rollouts — product wants the ability to set a canary that only affects fallbacks, e.g., enterprise pin to large-v2 but let pro fallback to med-v1 during peak. Need console controls to visualize fallback ratio and enforce a max fallback rate per shard.

sarah: Agree. Dashboard: show "fallback ratio" time series, per-tier and per-region heatmap. Also add alert rule: fallback_ratio > 20% for 5m => page SRE. For free tier maybe don't page, just log.

eliz: For quota enforcement semantics — clarify terms: soft = throttle + best_effort fallback, best_effort = prefer preferred models but no hard reject, hard = reject with 429. We should document and standardize these names.

mike: There's also cost accounting implications. If a free tier request falls back to a more expensive model (e.g., due to geo routing), billing needs to use original tier pricing or actual model cost? ops/product decision.

tara: Product: free tier should never be billed higher, system must prefer cheaper variants not more expensive ones. If a fallback would increase cost, reject instead. Only pro/enterprise can be billed up or absorb more expensive fallback.

raj: Implementation note — fallback_budget should be implemented as token-bucket per tier-region pair and emitted as metric fallback_budget_remaining. Also add a counter fallback_attempts_total{tier,region,reason}.

mike: We'll need a migration path for existing policies. If no per-tier section, default to previous global policy with quota_enforcement: best_effort. Backwards compatible.

eliz: Also include a rolling window for telemetry to avoid noise: emit fallback_used only on first fallback per request, and aggregate per 10s for dashboards.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: routing-config-service v3.2 -> staging. If changes land, run migrations: /scripts/migrate-routing-v3.sh :rocket:

tara: next steps: mike + raj to prototype API response metadata and token-bucket enforcement. sarah to wire a mockup for the console panel (toggle + advanced budget). eliz to draft telemetry event schema and alert rules. I'll coordinate docs and product decisions on billing.

mike: I'll post a short PR with the API contract and an integration test. ETA 2 days.

raj: I'll start on the token-bucket and per-region counters.

sarah: I'll drop a Figma link in the thread tomorrow and annotate.

eliz: will draft the Prom/metric names: redwood_routing_fallback_budget_remaining, redwood_routing_fallback_used_total, redwood_routing_quota_rejected_total.

tara: perfect. Thanks all :raised_hands:

mike: one more: need docs for SDKs so that SDK callers can read metadata.routes to surface 'served_by' on the client. I can add that to the PR.

raj: note for follow-up: region-aware model affinity can cause oscillations — we should simulate traffic in staging with synthetic tenants before enabling budgets globally.

tara: added to action list. closing thread for now, will reopen once PRs are up.
